note: Design and marketing SUGGESTIONS for making this site read like a polished marketing affiliate website, plus the questions that must be answered before any of them is implemented. Every row that states a fact carries an official source ID from data/sources.json; every row that is a proposal is labelled as a proposal and is not a verified fact. Nothing unverified is inferred or filled in: where a value cannot be confirmed from an official source it is left blank and flagged. Suggestions here are published for review and decision; none is implemented by this session.

statuses.proposed: Published here for review. Not implemented. Implementation starts only after a decision is recorded.

verified_basis.item: Price, availability and review display rules
verified_basis.value: Participation Requirements 2(b) allow prices and availability on a site only when Amazon serves the link or the data comes from the Creators API or PA API; 6(t) allows customer reviews and star ratings only through the Creators API or PA API.

verified_basis.item: Special Links must carry the Associates tag

suggestions.title: Brand and hero treatment for the landing page
suggestions.what: Give the site a marketing name, a one-line promise and a hero section that leads with the three air-fryer products and what a reader gets (comparisons, buying guides, verified specs). Use Amazon-provided Program Content (images, link formats) served through the link, not scraped screenshots.
suggestions.why: A polished marketing site starts with one clear promise above the fold. Amazon's Operating Agreement makes Program Content (data, images, text, link formats, widgets) available to Associates, so official assets can be used without inventing product photography.

compliance.text: Program Content is made available for advertising items; it excludes product data from non-Amazon sites.

suggestions.implementation_2026_11_16: The Crisp Report — a named masthead, a one-line promise and a hero that leads with the three listings and the reader's payoff. Built on this branch; the dashboard's own landing hero is unchanged.

suggestions.title: Editorial article hub built from the verified topic plan
suggestions.what: Publish the 12 working article titles already planned on the Content topics page as real articles: a hub listing them with working titles, the verified Amazon fact each rests on, and a short summary. Give each article a byline, a date and a 'what we verified / what we did not' note.
suggestions.why: Catchy, topic-driven articles are the main organic-traffic lever for an affiliate site, and the topic plan already anchors every title to a fact printed on the listing, so the content has something real to say instead of generic filler.

compliance.text: No topic may state a price, star rating or review count unless Amazon serves the link or the data comes from the API.
No topic may claim search volume, trend direction or conversion data: Amazon publishes no such affiliate endpoint.

suggestions.implementation_2026_11_16: Six articles published in the /read/ section, each built on the fact-basis in this file and each claim footnoted to an official page: capacity arithmetic, feature taxonomy, the dishwasher-safe reading, a dated best-seller rank, how to read a listing title, and how the site gets paid.
suggestions.implementation_files_2026_11_16: read/capacity.html, read/features.html, read/cleaning.html, read/bestseller.html, read/listing-titles.html, read/getting-paid.html

suggestions.title: Human-review gate to remove the AI-slop feel
suggestions.what: Before publication, every article passes a review checklist: specific verified specs, no generic filler, no invented experience, the disclosure shown near the recommendation, and a named reviewer. A short 'how this was written' note states which facts were read from which Amazon page.
suggestions.why: The brief asks that the site not read like AI slop. The most defensible way to achieve that without inventing claims is a visible editorial process: every statement traces to an Amazon page, and every article says what was and was not verified.

compliance.text: FTC: you cannot talk about your experience with a product you have not tried.
FTC: the disclosure must be hard to miss and placed close to the recommendation; an 'affiliate link' label or a buy button alone is not an adequate disclosure.

suggestions.implementation_2026_11_16: Anti-slop craft applied at generation time: a named voice, sentence-shaped subheads, concrete numbers only, no filler adjectives, an admission on every page that nothing was tested. A NAMED human reviewer and a publish-after-sign-off gate still cannot be built without an owner decision (Q5).

suggestions.title: Comparison and buying-guide pages in marketing style
suggestions.what: Restyle the existing comparison and buying-guide pages (marketing/comparison.html, marketing/buying-guide.html) with a clear comparison matrix and a 'who this is for' buying guide, using only verified listing attributes (capacity, features, brand) from the destination page titles.
suggestions.why: Comparisons and buying guides are the highest-intent content for air fryer buyers and convert readers into clicks; a clean matrix plus a decision guide reads like a real marketing site rather than a data dump.

compliance.text: Prices, availability, ratings and review counts may appear only when Amazon serves the link or the data comes from the Creators API or PA API.

suggestions.implementation_2026_11_16: A consumer-shaped comparison table (13 attributes, sourced inside each cell, blanks left where the listing does not say) and a five-question buying guide with an FAQ block.

suggestions.title: Conversion-oriented calls to action with tagged Special Links
suggestions.what: Add clear 'Check price on Amazon' style calls to action that point to Amazon through the owner's tagged Special Links, with the disclosure adjacent to each CTA.
suggestions.why: Marketing sites convert through clear next steps. This depends entirely on the owner supplying the Associates tag; without it no link earns commission.

compliance.text: Every Special Link must carry the Associates tag (Participation Requirements 2(b)).
FTC: a 'buy now' button alone is not an adequate disclosure.

suggestions.blocker: The Associates tag is not known to this session (FLG-010). Implementation waits on owner input Q1.
suggestions.implementation_2026_11_16: CTA buttons are placed on every product card and on the comparison page, each opening the official Amazon listing and marked rel="nofollow sponsored". They CANNOT earn until an Associates tag exists, so no Special Link is published. The blocker is unchanged: participation requirement 2(b).

suggestions.title: Trust section: how the site stays accurate
suggestions.what: Add a trust section explaining the verification protocol: every value comes from an official Amazon or FTC page, unverified cells stay blank, and the Flagged for review page publishes open items with their source links.
suggestions.why: Affiliate trust is a conversion factor. The site already has a verification discipline; presenting it plainly distinguishes it from sloppy AI sites and answers the credibility question before a reader clicks.

compliance.text: Operating Agreement Section 5 disclosure wording must remain prominent wherever Program Content is used.

suggestions.implementation_2026_11_16: A four-rule trust strip on the front page, a disclosure strip above the masthead on every page, and a method page that publishes the pipeline plus the questions this site cannot answer.

suggestions.title: SEO mechanics with honest meta descriptions
suggestions.what: Keep the generated meta descriptions, canonical links and sitemap, and add article-level metadata when articles are published. Meta descriptions state what the page is and never claim metrics that cannot be sourced.
suggestions.why: Clean metadata and a current sitemap are the baseline for organic traffic and are already generated by the build; extending them to articles costs little and keeps every claim traceable.

compliance.text: No search-volume, trend or conversion claims are made because no official source publishes them for affiliates.

suggestions.implementation_2026_11_16: Unique title and meta description per page, canonical URL, Open Graph and Twitter card, JSON-LD (WebSite, Article with dates and publisher, ItemList, BreadcrumbList, CollectionPage, FAQPage, Table, HowTo), semantic h1/h2 structure, descriptive link text, sitemap regenerated from the live tree, robots already pointing at it.

suggestions.title: Trending-topics section anchored to point-in-time official surfaces
suggestions.what: Add an editorial 'in the kitchen now' style section that points to what the listings themselves show (verified attributes and the Amazon Best Sellers page as a point-in-time reference), rather than asserting trends.
suggestions.why: The brief asks for trendy topics. A trend claim with no source is exactly the AI-slop the brief wants avoided; anchoring to a named, dated official surface keeps the section honest and still feels current.

compliance.text: Amazon's category Best Sellers page is the only official popularity surface; it is point-in-time and moves between captures.
No search-volume or trend-direction claims may be made.

suggestions.implementation_2026_11_16: A trend article that publishes one dated rank from Amazon's own Best Sellers in Air Fryers page, explains what a rank is not, and documents the title-drift evidence between captures instead of smoothing it.

suggestions.title: Click and conversion tracking through Amazon's own reporting
suggestions.what: Track clicks and conversions using the reporting Amazon provides to Associates, and record campaign performance in the Campaigns ledger only from those sources. Do not add third-party link-tracking that could create artificial sessions.
suggestions.why: The brief requires click/conversion tracking and continuous optimization. Amazon's own reporting is the compliant data path; it also feeds the ledger with values that can be sourced rather than guessed.

compliance.text: Participation Requirements prohibit artificial clicks or sessions.

suggestions.implementation_2026_11_16: No analytics, no consent banner and no JavaScript were added, deliberately: with no tag there is nothing to attribute a conversion to, and adding a third-party tracker first would create a consent obligation the site does not need yet. Awaiting the owner's stack decision (Q8).

suggestions.title: Content cadence and a named editor before scaling articles
suggestions.what: Agree a publishing cadence and a named reviewer for the article hub before scaling it, and record each decision on the coordination board so implementation is traceable.
suggestions.why: Scaling content without a review gate is how sites acquire the AI-slop reputation the brief wants avoided; a cadence plus named owner makes the editorial process real rather than cosmetic.

compliance.text: FTC guidance on experience claims applies to any first-person content.

suggestions.implementation_2026_11_16: A cadence and a named reviewer are owner decisions. The scaffolding that a cadence needs — a generator that refuses to publish an uncited row — is now in place, so a schedule can be added without new tooling.

questions.question: What is the Associates tag (tracking ID) to use on every Special Link?
questions.what_we_know: Every Special Link must carry the Associates tag; without it no link on the site is trackable for commissions.
questions.what_we_dont_know: The tag value. No document read in this project contains it.
questions.why_it_matters: Blocks SUG-05 (CTAs) and every commission-earning link on the site.
questions.how_to_discover: Owner supplies the tag from Associates Central. Record it in the coordination log; do not store it in public files.

questions.question: Are the three destination listings the products that were intended?
questions.what_we_know: Each submitted short link opens a specific live listing: B0CDY277D3, B09B7SB46R, B08DKYBTPH. The mapping is stable across captures by three sessions, but no official source ties the links to the intended products.
questions.what_we_dont_know: The owner's intent behind the three submitted links.
questions.why_it_matters: All product content, comparisons and buying guides depend on identity. Wrong identity means the site promotes products the owner did not choose.
questions.how_to_discover: Owner confirms the three intended ASINs. If the intended products differ, re-run the intake and re-verify before any content is published.

questions.question: Which Amazon marketplace is the site for?
questions.what_we_know: Operating Agreement Schedule 1 lists one location for this agreement text: United States, amazon.com. Commission tables are per-locale.
questions.what_we_dont_know: Whether the owner wants to target other locales or stay US-only.
questions.why_it_matters: Links, rates and eligible products differ per marketplace; the site's current data is US-only.
questions.how_to_discover: Owner decision. If other locales are wanted, each needs its own verified commission table and link set before content is written.

questions.question: Is the Associates account enrolled, and does it meet the Creators API prerequisites?
questions.what_we_know: The Creators API requires enrolment and at least 10 qualifying sales within the past 30 days; the application review requires three qualifying sales in 180 days and excludes personal orders.
questions.what_we_dont_know: The account's enrolment status and sales history.
questions.why_it_matters: Price, availability, ratings and review counts can only appear on the site when Amazon serves the link or the data comes from the Creators API or PA API. Without API access those cells stay blank.
questions.how_to_discover: Owner checks Associates Central. Record the result; the site's blank cells are the fallback until then.

questions.question: Who reviews and publishes content, and at what cadence?
questions.what_we_know: The site already publishes a verification protocol and a flagged-for-review process.
questions.what_we_dont_know: The owner's cadence and named reviewer.
questions.why_it_matters: The human-review gate (SUG-03) is the main defence against the AI-slop feel; without a real reviewer it is cosmetic.
questions.how_to_discover: Owner assigns a reviewer and a cadence; record the decision before scaling the article hub.

questions.question: Will the products be used or tested first-hand?
questions.what_we_know: FTC guidance states you cannot talk about your experience with a product you have not tried.
questions.what_we_dont_know: Whether the owner will purchase or test the three products.
questions.why_it_matters: Determines whether first-person 'we tested' style content is allowed. Without first-hand use, all content must stay attribute-and-fact based.
questions.how_to_discover: Owner decision. If no testing, the editorial rule stays: only verified listing facts and official document facts.

questions.question: What brand direction (name, palette, voice) should the marketing site use?
questions.what_we_know: Nothing official restricts the site's own brand; the only mandated text is the Associates disclosure.
questions.what_we_dont_know: The owner's preferred name, colors and tone.
questions.why_it_matters: Drives the polished-marketing look (SUG-01) and all page styling.
questions.how_to_discover: Owner picks from options or supplies brand assets; record the choice in the coordination log before implementation.

questions.question: Which analytics and reporting stack will be used for clicks and conversions?
questions.what_we_know: Amazon provides reporting to Associates; participation requirements prohibit artificial clicks or sessions.
questions.what_we_dont_know: The owner's preference and any third-party tooling.
questions.why_it_matters: Determines how the Campaigns ledger gets real values and how optimization is measured.
questions.how_to_discover: Owner decision, reviewed against Program Policies before any third-party tool is added.

questions.question: What budget and tooling exist for keyword and topic research?
questions.what_we_know: Amazon publishes no affiliate search-volume, keyword-difficulty or conversion-rate data, so no such claim can be made on the site.
questions.what_we_dont_know: The owner's budget and preferred tools.
questions.why_it_matters: Determines how article priority is decided; external keyword tools can suggest topics but their numbers must never be presented as Amazon facts.
questions.how_to_discover: Owner supplies budget/tools; record which tools are approved before use.

questions.question: Should the disclosure placement be reviewed by counsel before launch?
questions.what_we_know: The required wording is fixed by the Operating Agreement; FTC guidance requires the disclosure to be clear, conspicuous and close to the recommendation.
questions.what_we_dont_know: Whether the owner wants a formal legal review.
questions.why_it_matters: Disclosure breaches are treated as a material breach of the agreement; placement decisions carry compliance weight.
questions.how_to_discover: Owner decision; if yes, review the disclosure pattern on every page template before publishing.

workflow: 1. Review this page with the suggestions (SUG-01 to SUG-10) and the open questions (Q1 to Q10) side by side.
2. Answer each open question from the owner; record the answer and its source or note that it is a decision, not a fact.
3. For each suggestion, choose Accept, Reject or Defer, and record the choice and the reason in COORDINATION.md under this session's part.
4. Only accepted suggestions are implemented, in a follow-up session that re-verifies the affected pages against official sources before publishing.
5. Blocked suggestions (currently SUG-05) stay blocked until the named blocker is resolved; nothing on this page is implemented by this session.

6. Status as of 2026-11-16 (session 145b8df7): PATH-A is implemented on branch arena/145b8df7-zone3 and published under /read/; PATH-B's owner input is still the single highest-value item on this page; PATH-C and PATH-D stay deferred for the reasons stated in their rows.

paths.label: Ship the editorial layer as the front door; keep the dashboard as the audit view
paths.what_it_buys: A site a person would read and re-link, with every claim checkable. Organic-traffic surface (articles, guides, FAQ, category hub, schema) without a single invented number.
paths.what_it_costs: Nothing further to publish; maintenance is a re-capture when a listing title or a commission table changes.
paths.risk_if_chosen: Low. The exposure is that it earns nothing until the tag exists, and that analysis-only copy converts worse than tested reviews.
paths.prerequisite: Accept the brand direction (Q7). Tag (Q1) converts it from a portfolio piece into a business.
paths.recommendation: Recommended default, and what this session implemented.

paths.label: Pause the marketing layer until the three product IDs are confirmed
paths.what_it_buys: Removes the largest correctness risk: the site currently describes the listings the links opened, which no official source ties to owner intent.
paths.what_it_costs: Delays everything else on an input that takes one message to supply.
paths.risk_if_chosen: If the intended products differ, six articles and the comparison table need re-writing. That re-work is cheap and already flagged.
paths.recommendation: Do this in parallel, not instead: the copy is written so that a wrong destination costs a rewrite, not a correction of policy.

paths.label: Invest in first-party testing and original photography
paths.what_it_buys: The only route to experience claims, and the only route to product imagery the site may legally own and store.
paths.what_it_costs: Sample units, a documented protocol, storage, and a real reviewer to sign off claims.
paths.risk_if_chosen: Highest legal and reputational risk if any claim outruns the protocol; FTC treatment of fake testing is the obvious hazard.
paths.prerequisite: Q6 (budget and protocol) and Q5 (who signs off).
paths.recommendation: Defer until the account earns. Do not fake it in the interim: the copy is written so no reader could mistake it for a test result, and SUG-03 only reaches full strength once a named reviewer signs off.

paths.label: Expand the niche before the first link works
paths.what_it_buys: More surface for organic traffic in theory.
paths.what_it_costs: Effort spent away from the two things that actually gate revenue: a tag and an approved account.
paths.risk_if_chosen: A larger unmonetised site, and more rows to re-verify by hand each time Amazon edits a title.
paths.prerequisite: None — which is exactly why it is tempting.
paths.recommendation: Not recommended until PATH-A and PATH-B are resolved.
